_source.paper: Liu et al., iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting, ICLR 2024
_source.note: This is the benchmark compilation that S-Mamba (Wang et al., Neurocomputing 2025) and ms-Mamba also report their baselines against. The S-Mamba paper itself was not retrievable in the build environment (arxiv.org, ScienceDirect and ACM are blocked by the network policy), so the baseline block is taken from the upstream compilation it reproduces. Transcribed from the published table image and verified twice at 2.6x magnification.
_source.granularity: Averages over H in {96,192,336,720}; PEMS over T in {12,24,48,96}. ETT and PEMS are averaged across their four datasets, which is how the source reports them.
_source.caveat: These figures come from a different codebase, preprocessing and seed set than this repository. They are NOT comparable to results/unified_*.json on a like-for-like basis. Re-running four of these baselines in our pipeline moves them by up to 0.017 MSE in either direction; see the reproduction_gap block below. Use for positioning only.

dd_mamba._source: results/Main_*.json / benchmark_pems_electricity.json, as reported in tab:horizons
dd_mamba._solar_note: Solar uses a test-informed normalization setting; exploratory only.

reproduction_gap._what: Same model, our pipeline (results/unified_*.json, 5 seeds) minus its published MSE. Quantifies the cross-pipeline confound in tab:published.
reproduction_gap._finding: Linear models transfer almost exactly; the deep baselines move most, consistent with published deep baselines carrying per-dataset tuning that one shared schedule does not reproduce.
